  1. Show HN: Alloy CSS, dialogs, menus and tabs that work with JavaScript off

    • Design
    • Software Development

    210 points · 38 comments · 17 Nov 2026, 15:07 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Alloy CSS is a fixed-scale CSS kit for server-rendered interfaces that uses current browser features such as dialog, popover, commandfor, and :has(). Its linked invoice-dashboard example is one HTML file with no JavaScript while retaining menus, dialog, drawer, tabs, tooltips, toast, and other interactions.

    Discussion — Supporters welcomed progressive enhancement and less client-side JavaScript. Skeptics raised accessibility, CSS-name conflicts, and complexity concerns; the author said Alloy is a new design system rather than a drop-in utility layer. Discussion also debated which browser capabilities should become native and where JavaScript remains necessary.

  2. Show HN: Fakemetrics.com – "build in public" like a superstar

    • Data Visualization
    • Design

    51 points · 22 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 18:08 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — FakeMetrics is a tool for making mock copies of familiar dashboards with explicitly made-up numbers for slides, demos, or jokes. The author described it as an experiment in screenshot-driven UI cloning.

    Discussion — Commenters discussed the ethics and possible misuse of fake dashboard screenshots, as well as the technical challenge of visually matching interfaces. The author asked whether UI-cloning work should become an open-source product.

  3. Show HN: A custom font based on the Jamaican flag alphabet

    • Design
    • Typography

    56 points · 9 comments · 15 Nov 2026, 00:56 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Jamaican Alphabet Font is an experimental font inspired by treating Jamaica’s flag as the letter X. It includes regular and connected variants, with colors and shapes encoded in the font and contextual features joining selected glyphs.

    Discussion — The short thread was positive. A commenter linked a fuller making-of post and asked about color choices; the author explained that alternate color variants exist but default rules avoid an overly stripey result.

  4. Show HN: Isometric SF – A pixel-art map of the SF Bay Area

    • Design
    • Maps

    256 points · 76 comments · 13 Nov 2026, 17:58 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — An interactive, isometric map of the San Francisco Bay Area rendered in a pixel-art-like visual style. The public landing page provides the map and a link to a making-of page, but exposes little implementation detail in its initial rendered text.

    Discussion — The dominant discussion was whether the imagery qualifies as pixel art: critics cited anti-aliasing and generative-image artifacts, while others praised the map and recognized locations. Commenters also asked for north-oriented or rotatable views; one identified Google photorealistic 3D tiles as the underlying imagery.
